title: Emporia Latency Percentiles
description: REWORK_NOTE Phase 1_3. All percentiles come from histogram buckets via histogram_quantile, never from averages or _sum/_count, and never from the _active_ long-task-timer families. Every latency panel has traffic volume and an outcome breakdown nearby, because a p99 over few samples is noise and a falling p99 during failures usually means the path stopped doing work. Metric names and labels were read from the running stack; see rework/PHASE_1_3_DISCOVERY.md.

list.name: deployment
list.label: Deployment
list.description: docker for the full-stack compose run, host for run-local.sh / run-infra-docker.sh.

panels.title: Order submit p99
panels.description: Thresholds from the Phase 1_2 baseline: at or below the ~40 orders/sec knee p99 stayed under ~100ms. Laptop-derived context, not a production SLO.

panels.title: Order submit rate
panels.description: Always read the percentile panels next to this. A p99 computed from a handful of samples is noise.

panels.title: Submit error + timeout ratio
panels.description: A falling p99 during failures can mean the path stopped doing work rather than got faster. Read them together.

panels.title: Kafka lag (stable groups)
panels.description: Broker-side exporter lag, clamped: the exporter reports -1 for partitions with no committed offset. Full detail on the Kafka Consumer Lag dashboard.

panels.title: Order submit latency
panels.description: Click an exemplar dot to open the matching trace in Tempo.

panels.title: Order submit rate by outcome
panels.description: Outcome vocabulary is open-ended: strategy paths also emit 'waiting', portfolio emits 'duplicate'. Do not assume only success/rejected/timeout/error.

panels.title: Submit latency by operation and destination

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, operation, destination) (rate(emporia_order_submit_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, operation, destination) (rate(emporia_order_submit_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, operation, destination) (rate(emporia_order_submit_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: Phase 1_2 traced ~1.2s of a 1.24s submit to waiting on the Kafka request/reply round trip, not to downstream processing.

panels.title: Risk check latency by service

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, service, decision) (rate(emporia_risk_check_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service, decision) (rate(emporia_risk_check_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, service, decision) (rate(emporia_risk_check_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: Grouped by service deliberately: emporia.risk.check is emitted by BOTH order-command-service (reason=permission) and order-management-service (reason=quantity|symbol). Without the service label two unrelated checks average into one line.

panels.title: Submit rate by operation, destination, outcome
Submit failures by outcome and error
panels.description: The error label (exception class name) is used here and only here. It is deliberately kept out of the percentile panels, where it would multiply series without adding meaning.

panels.title: Command handle rate by outcome
panels.description: outcome=duplicate means the idempotency cache answered, which is the retry path working as intended.

panels.title: JDBC query latency by service
panels.description: jdbc_query_seconds_bucket, not jdbc_query_active_seconds_bucket. The _active_ family is a long-task timer measuring work still in flight, and produces plausible-looking but wrong percentiles.

panels.title: Kafka listener processing latency by consumer group

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, service, messaging_kafka_consumer_group) (rate(spring_kafka_listener_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service, messaging_kafka_consumer_group) (rate(spring_kafka_listener_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, service, messaging_kafka_consumer_group) (rate(spring_kafka_listener_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: spring_kafka_* metrics carry messaging_kafka_consumer_group and report each topic once. The dotted/underscored duplication and the topic=~"emporia\\..+" filter apply to kafka_consumer_* client metrics only; the label here is messaging_source_name, so that filter would match nothing.

panels.title: Strategy decision latency
panels.description: Absent until a SMART or VWAP order runs: Micrometer creates a meter on first observation, so an unexercised path shows No data rather than zero.

panels.title: Venue operation latency

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, venue_mode, operation) (rate(emporia_execution_venue_operation_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, venue_mode, operation) (rate(emporia_execution_venue_operation_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, venue_mode, operation) (rate(emporia_execution_venue_operation_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: exchange-core checkpoints synchronously to disk on every submit/replace/cancel, so this includes that durability cost.

panels.title: Strategy decision rate by outcome
panels.description: outcome=waiting dominates in normal operation (a tick that decided to do nothing yet). A success rate computed against the four declared outcomes would read wrong.

panels.title: Snapshot apply latency
panels.description: Requires an actual fill to appear. Every order in the local load scripts is a BUY, so with no resting SELL liquidity nothing fills and this panel stays empty. No data here does not imply a broken query.

panels.title: Snapshot apply rate by outcome
panels.description: outcome=duplicate is a documented extension: a snapshot already applied.

panels.title: HTTP server latency by route

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, service, method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service, method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, service, method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: uri is the templated route (/instruments/{id}), never a raw URL, so cardinality stays bounded.

panels.title: HTTP client latency by target

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, service, client_name, uri) (rate(http_client_requests_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service, client_name, uri) (rate(http_client_requests_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, service, client_name, uri) (rate(http_client_requests_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: Requires spring-boot-starter-restclient; without it there is no auto-configured RestClient.Builder, no observation, and this panel is silently empty. The uri tag comes from the URI *template*, so a pre-built URL string would unbound cardinality here.

panels.title: Order submit p99 against the measured knee
panels.description: Phase 1_2 measured: <=40 orders/sec p99 under ~100ms with lag ~0; 48/sec p50 3137ms with sustained lag 123-199; 80/sec 7.7% infra failures. These are one laptop's numbers and warning-only context.

panels.title: Stable-group lag beside submit p99
panels.description: Lag climbing while p99 climbs indicates consumers falling behind rather than a slow single request.

panels.title: Accepted rate vs failure rate
panels.description: Throughput collapsing while latency looks fine is the signature of the system failing closed.
